This TEMPORARY position through our Temporary Office of the President Staffing program.

Reporting to Chief of Staff (COS), the Senior Finance and Resource Manager oversees and is accountable for all aspects of division finance, including the division’s financial accounting, operating budget and forecasts; financial activities for LBNL and the special purpose entities managing LANL and LLNL; LBNL Home Office Costs (HOC) annual proposal, audit, and compliance; UCNL operating and reserve fund management; and faculty and consultant billing and reimbursement.

[50%] UCNL Budget Development and Financial Management: Responsibilities include the administration of a complex budget with multiple financial units; fiscal administration and controls; oversight of resource allocation. Develop the division’s annual revenue and expense budget and report quarterly forecast. Review monthly budget-to-actual reports to monitor budget and financial activity on a regular basis. Responsible for ensuring that expenses do not exceed the approved budget, and that all transactions are processed in compliance with university policies and procedures. Coordinate with the UCOP Budget and Finance Office (BFO) to evaluate budget strategy to meet UCNL short-term and long-term strategic planning.

Responsible for month-end close, quarterly forecast, and year-end close financial transactions. Prepare annual Budget vs. Actual analysis and present to UCNL division. Collaborate with UCNL leaders and UC campuses on Inter-location Transfers of Fund (ITFs), as well as fund transfers to/from UC’s affiliated National Laboratories and the federal government. Provide financial expertise to the division on various financial policies and procedures. Provide UCNL leadership regular detailed, actionable financial reports for division. Manage and oversee budgets and expenditures for UCNL projects and programs.

[30%] LBNL Financial Management: Manage fee earned by UC under LBNL prime contract (UC Management Fee) and unallowable expenses. Partner with LBNL Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Office to develop LBNL Management Report and record UC earned revenue and unallowable expenses to UC financial system. Reconcile UC Management Fee after DOE issues annual performance rating. Reconcile LBNL net fee and execute related communications and financial transfers. Manage funds related to debt servicing of capital projects and to operation of LBNL guest house. Act as the division's financial liaison to the Berkeley Lab Foundation.

[5%] LANL/LLNL Financial Management: Manage fee revenue earned by UC for managing LANL and LLNL via special purpose entities. Record UC earned revenue and unallowable expenses to UC financial system. Prepare annual spend plan for Regental approval on allocation of estimated LANL and LLNL fee and prepare annual spend plan reconciliation based on actual fee.

[5%] LBNL Home Office Costs (HOC) Proposal Development: Lead development of annual LBNL HOC proposal in collaboration with UCNL staff and various UCOP divisions and departments. Partner with UCOP BFO and departments on annual HOC budget request. Apply different methodology and use complex Excel models to exclude Federal unallowable costs. Compile funding requests from UCNL and UCOP departments to develop annual HOC proposal for UCNL Executive Director’s review and approval to submit to DOE Site Office for final approval.

[10%] LBNL HOC Audit Administration: Responsible for the annual audit process. Prepare HOC reports as requested. Coordinate with LBNL CFO Office, UCOP BFO, and UC Controller’s Office to respond to LBNL auditor’s Request for Documentation (RFD) and provide documentation to audit testing samples. Provide the auditor with the UCNL annual allocation rate and UCNL staff labor certification letters. Explore ways to improve efficiencies of audit process. Prepare financial journals to transfer HOC fund to UCOP indirect cost fund.
Minimum 8 years of relevant experience in providing sophisticated, mission-critical services, including budget, finance, operations and/or human resources.
Expert knowledge of finance policies, practices, and systems.
Ability to identify, collect, analyze, and report on complex data.
Expert ability to effectively communicate complex information to executive leadership and management both verbally and in writing in a clear and concise manner.

Expert ability using multiple spreadsheet and database software tools to synthesize and integrate information for highly complex, strategic financial analysis, fiscal management, and financial reports.
Expert knowledge and understanding of federal government agency requirements and UC/DOE contracts.
